What You Can Expect

A good remodel begins with a good process. We start with clarity, not pressure.

A practical discussion about your home and priorities
Clear direction on scope, timing, and next steps
One accountable team from planning through final walkthrough
REQUEST A CONSULTATION
Let’s Start With
Your Project.

Share a few details below and our team will follow up to schedule a complimentary consultation. This is the only online submission form on the Bayshore Remodels website.

By submitting this form, you agree to our Privacy Policy and Terms of Service. Prefer to reach us directly? Call (813) 489-1552.

NO SURPRISES
What Happens After
You Hit Submit.

Here is exactly what to expect, step by step.

We reach out within one business day

Our office calls or texts you back to set up a time to talk.

A quick call

What you want to change, your timeline and a ballpark budget. If we’re not the right fit, we’ll tell you then and point you to someone who is.

Free consultation at your home

About 30 minutes. We look at the space, measure, check what’s behind the work (plumbing, electrical, condition) and talk through options.

Your written estimate

The work broken out by trade, what’s included, what’s a selection, and a timeline. Usually within a day for smaller jobs, a few days for design projects. No obligation.

You decide

No pressure and no pushy follow-ups. If you move forward, we plan selections and order materials before anything is torn out.

Nothing to worry about.

Sending the form doesn’t commit you to anything. There’s no high-pressure sales visit and no endless follow-up calls. We use your information only to talk with you about your project.

GOOD TO KNOW BEFORE WE TALK
Real Prices,
Up Front.

So you know whether we’re in your range before you ever call. See the full pricing FAQ →

Kitchens from
$28,000
Bathrooms from
$15,500
Cabinets from
$5,000
Whole home from
$150,000
Have a budget in mind?

Tell us. It isn’t a trap; it helps us show you what fits and what to hold off on.

Photos help

A few phone photos of the space let us come to the consultation better prepared.

Not sure what you need?

That’s fine. Many people start with a problem, not a plan. We’ll help sort it out.

OUR TERMS IN PLAIN ENGLISH
How We Work
Together.

The short version of what you can count on from us.

Consultations are free. No charge to meet, measure and talk options.
Your written estimate is the price. The ranges on this site help you plan; your estimate is what your project is priced on, and its price holds for 30 days.
Changes are approved in writing first. Anything you add, and any hidden condition we find, is priced and approved before the work happens.
Permits when required. We pull them and the work meets current code.
Your own materials are welcome. They need to be on site before the trades need them; our warranty covers the installation.
1-year written workmanship warranty. Paint carries a 2-year warranty against blistering and peeling, and products carry the manufacturer warranty.
Deposit, then progress payments. A deposit gets you on the schedule; the rest is paid in draws as the work progresses, so you never pay far ahead of the work.
One project manager. One person to call from planning through the final walkthrough.
Licensed and insured. Florida residential contractor CRC1335471.

Your signed agreement contains the full terms, including the exact deposit and payment schedule. We walk through it with you line by line before you sign, and you can ask about anything.

NO PRESSURE. JUST A CLEAR NEXT STEP.
Your Home Deserves
a Thoughtful Plan.

Bring us the questions, the inspiration, and the space that no longer works. We will bring the experience to help you move forward with confidence.

Kitchen Remodeling

New cabinets and countertops are included in every kitchen range below.

Semi-Custom to Custom

Semi-custom or custom cabinetry, larger kitchens and layout changes.

On site once work starts: small kitchens 3 to 5 weeks, full kitchens 4 to 6 weeks, semi-custom to custom 6 to 10 weeks.

HOW WE WORK
No Sales Pitch.
Just How It Actually Goes.

Who we’re a good fit for, who we’re not, how a project runs from the first call to the final walkthrough, and the terms we hold ourselves to. If something here doesn’t sit right with you, better you know now.

Are We the Right Fit?

We’d rather tell you up front than waste your time, or ours.

We’re a great fit if…
Your project involves three or more trades, like plumbing, electrical, tile and cabinets. That’s where a general contractor earns their keep.
You want it done right and permitted, not just done cheap.
You’re planning a kitchen from $28,000, a bathroom from $15,500, cabinets from $5,000 or a whole home from $150,000.
You live in Pinellas, Hillsborough or Pasco. We take on select Sarasota and Lakewood Ranch projects when the job makes sense.
You want one person to call, a written scope and no surprises.
We’re probably not the right fit if…
You only need one trade, like an interior paint job or new soffits. You can hire that trade directly, and we’re happy to refer the subs we trust.
You’re looking for the lowest number no matter what’s behind it.
You’d rather manage the trades and judge the work yourself. That’s a fair choice, and some homeowners do it well.

Not sure whether you need a contractor at all? Ask us. We’ll tell you honestly.

“Everybody is specialized and they only do what they do. There’s no guy jack-of-all-trading in there.”
JUSTIN, OWNER

Every stage of your project is done by someone who only does that trade, with at least 10 years in it, coordinated by one project manager. Specialists move faster and cleaner through their stage, and that’s a big part of how we keep a schedule.

Demolition
Licensed plumbing
Licensed electrical
Drywall
Tile

Countertops

If You’ve Been Burned by a Contractor Before

We hear it all the time: paid a lot up front and the job dragged on, the contractor disappeared, the price kept climbing, nobody called back. Here’s how we’re set up differently.

How we’re set up
A deposit, then progress payments. You pay as the work gets done, never far ahead of it.
Materials before demolition. Cabinets, tile and fixtures are ordered and on the way before anything comes out, so your kitchen never sits gutted.
One project manager. One person to call from planning through the walkthrough.
A written scope, broken out by trade. You know exactly what you’re paying for.
When something comes up
Things come up on every remodel. Rot behind a dishwasher, two layers of old flooring, wiring that isn’t to code.
When we find something, we stop, show you, and price it in writing before any extra work happens.
What keeps a timeline isn’t luck. It’s preparing properly and walking down that road before work starts: selections made, materials on site, trades sequenced, inspections planned in.
Why We Ask About Your Budget

It isn’t so we can spend all of it. Knowing your number tells us what’s realistic, so we can build a package that fits: the right scope, the right materials and the right finish level for what you want to spend. If what you want and what you want to spend don’t line up, we’ll tell you before you’ve paid for anything. See what projects cost.

How a Project Goes

From the first call to the final walkthrough.

A quick call

We reach out within one business day. What you want to change, your timeline and a ballpark budget.

Free 30-minute consultation

At your home. We look at the space, measure and check what’s behind the work.

Your written estimate

Broken out by trade. Usually within a day for smaller jobs, a few days for design projects.

Design & selections

A 3D rendering on every kitchen, and on bathrooms when you want one. Every selection made before we start.

Order, then build

Materials ordered and confirmed first. Then each specialist does their stage, in order.

Walkthrough & warranty

We walk it with you, close out every punch-list item, and put the warranty in writing.

Our Terms in Plain English

The short version of what you can hold us to.

Consultations are free. So is the written estimate.
Your estimate is the price. It holds for 30 days.
Changes are approved in writing first. Always.
Permits when required. Permitted work meets today’s code, which costs more and protects you when you sell.
Your own materials are welcome. They need to be on site before the trades need them.
1-year written workmanship warranty. Products carry the manufacturer warranty.
Paint: 2 years against blistering and peeling, plus a 30-day touch-up visit.
Licensed and insured. Florida residential contractor CRC1335471.
Family Owned. Faith First. Giving Back.

A few things about who we are that don’t fit on an estimate.

Family owned and operated

When you call, you’re talking to the family that owns the company, not a call center or a franchise. Your project matters to us because our name is on it.

Faith first

Our faith shapes how we run this business: tell people the truth, price fairly, keep our word, and treat your home the way we’d want ours treated.

Giving back to animal rescues

Animal rescues are close to our hearts. We support Rescue Dogs Dream, an all-volunteer dog rescue from Justin’s hometown that takes in at-risk, senior and sick shelter dogs and cares for them until they find a home.

What Our Customers Say

Refinish, Reface or Remodel?
How to Choose for Your Kitchen.

Three questions decide it. Here’s how we walk Tampa Bay homeowners through the choice, with real prices, timelines and what each option can’t do.

Find Your Answer
Ask Us to Look
The short answer

If your cabinet boxes are solid and you like your layout, you don’t need a remodel. Keep your door style and change the color with refinishing, from $5,000. Change the door style with refacing, from $7,000. If the layout doesn’t work or the boxes are failing, a kitchen remodel, from $28,000, is the better spend.

THREE QUESTIONS
Answer These in Order
1. Are your cabinet boxes solid?

Look under the sink for water damage, check for sagging shelves, and see whether doors still hang straight.

If the boxes are damaged or failing, refinishing and refacing won’t fix that. You’re looking at a kitchen remodel.

2. Do you like your layout?

If you want to move cabinets, open a wall or add an island, that’s a kitchen remodel.

If you only want to add a cabinet or two, refacing can do it, with new countertops as part of the project.

3. Do you like your door style?

Yes: refinishing. Your doors are sprayed in our shop with a new color and a factory-style finish.

No, or the doors are thermofoil or peeling laminate: refacing. New doors and drawer fronts on the boxes you already have, with soft-close hinges and drawer slides standard.

SIDE BY SIDE
How the Three Options Compare
	REFINISHING	REFACING	FULL KITCHEN REMODEL
What changes	Color and finish	Door and drawer style, plus finish	Everything, including the layout
Countertops	Optional. Keep yours or replace them	Optional, unless we add a cabinet or two	Always replaced, and included in our ranges
Starting price	From $5,000	From $7,000	From $28,000
Most medium kitchens	$8,000–$10,000	$10,000–$12,500	$36,000–$50,000
Time on site	5 to 7 working days	5 to 7 working days	3 to 10 weeks
Warranty	2-year finish, 1-year workmanship	2-year finish, 1-year workmanship	1-year workmanship
Best when	Boxes and doors are solid and you like the style	Boxes are solid but you want a new door style	The layout or the cabinet boxes no longer work

Typical ranges from our recent projects, to help you plan. Your written estimate, built after we see your space, is what your project is priced on.

The countertop rule

With refinishing and refacing, keeping your countertops is your choice. Add a cabinet or two during refacing and new countertops become part of the project. With a full remodel, new countertops are always included. Whenever countertops change, they go in before any cabinet work.

HONEST LIMITS
What Each Option Can’t Do
Refinishing
It won’t change your door style or fix damaged boxes.
The finish lasts when the prep is right. Poor prep is why refinished cabinets peel, so we degrease, sand and prime every surface, and warranty against blistering and peeling for two years.
Refacing
It depends on sound cabinet boxes. Water-damaged or failing boxes aren’t good candidates.
It can add a cabinet or two, not move them. A new layout is a remodel.
Kitchen remodel
It takes the longest: 3 to 10 weeks on site, after cabinet lead times.
Walls and floors can hide damage you only find at demolition. We order materials first so your kitchen isn’t torn out while you wait.

What a Well-Planned Remodel Should Feel Like
JUN 25 
WRITTEN BY MICHAEL KUHN

“That is why we believe remodeling should feel like a partnership. At Treasure Valley Redesign & Remodel, we work with homeowners to balance their needs, their dreams, and their budget. Our role is to bring construction knowledge, design experience, planning, and coordination to the ideas and priorities you bring to the project.”

A good remodel does not begin with demolition; it begins when the things that are not working in your home, the ideas you have been carrying around, and the budget you have available start becoming a plan you can understand.

The finished space matters. You may be imagining a kitchen where everyone can gather comfortably, a bathroom that makes mornings easier, or a layout that simply works better for your family, but the experience getting there matters too.

Remodeling will always involve decisions and disruption. For a while, your home may feel less convenient before it becomes more comfortable. A well-planned remodel, though, should not leave you constantly guessing, reacting, or trying to manage the project on your own.

It should feel like you have a knowledgeable partner helping turn your ideas into a home that works better for the way you live.

It Begins With Being Heard

A good remodeling conversation starts with more than measurements, materials, and a list of rooms.

It starts with understanding what is not working and what you hope will be different when the project is complete.

Maybe your kitchen has enough square footage, but everyone still ends up crowded into the same corner. Maybe your bathroom looks dated, but the larger frustration is a lack of useful storage. Maybe you want to host family more often, stay comfortably in your home as you get older, or make everyday routines feel a little easier.

Good planning is not about fitting your ideas into a standard package. It is about understanding your needs, your dreams for the space, and the budget you are comfortable working within.

Before anyone starts proposing solutions, you should feel like they understand the problem you are trying to solve.

A Clear Plan Creates Confidence

The planning stage is where ideas begin becoming real: Layouts take shape, priorities become clearer, materials and finishes start working together, and questions that once felt overwhelming become a series of manageable decisions.

You do not need to understand every technical detail of construction. But before the work begins, you should have a clear picture of what is being built, what is included, and which decisions still need to be made. That gives you time to consider how the pieces work together.

It is much easier to compare cabinet layouts, plumbing fixtures, flooring, or tile when you are not being rushed for an immediate answer. Thoughtful decisions usually work together better than choices made because construction is waiting.

A clear plan does not mean every possible surprise can be eliminated. Existing homes sometimes reveal things no one could see beforehand. But good planning allows the team to address the things that can be known before construction begins, rather than leaving every detail to be figured out along the way.

Your Budget Becomes Part of the Design

Talking honestly about budget does not have to take the excitement out of remodeling.

A realistic budget helps the team understand where to focus, what is possible, and which choices will have the greatest effect on the finished space.

Sometimes an upgrade meaningfully improves the way a room functions. Other times, a simpler option may look beautiful, perform well, and leave more room for something your family will appreciate every day.

The goal is not to spend as much as possible. It is to use the investment thoughtfully.

That may mean protecting the features that matter most, simplifying something less important, or saving part of a larger vision for a future phase.

A good remodeling partner should help you understand those choices without making you feel pressured. The best solution is not always the most expensive one. It is the one that creates the right balance for your home and your family.

Communication Makes Construction Manageable

Even with careful planning, construction will change your normal routine. Parts of the house may be unavailable. Some days will be noisy. Progress may happen behind the walls before there is anything exciting to see.

Clear communication makes that much easier to manage.

You should know who to contact and feel comfortable asking questions. You should understand what has been completed, what is coming next, and whether the team needs anything from you.

Homeowners are not expected to automatically understand the construction process. Part of the remodeling team’s job is helping you understand the parts that affect you, your home, and your family.

Construction will still bring inconvenience. Good communication keeps that inconvenience from becoming unnecessary confusion.

In the End, It Should Still Feel Like Your Home

There is something special about watching a home change.

At first, demolition may make the project feel farther from completion than when it began. Then the new layout starts to appear. Walls are framed. Plumbing and electrical take shape. Cabinets arrive. The materials you selected begin coming together.

Slowly, the drawings and conversations become a real space.

You may see natural light reaching a part of the house that used to feel dark. You may stand where a new island will go and imagine your family gathered around it. You may watch an awkward corner become useful storage or a cramped room begin to feel open and comfortable.

Construction is not always pretty while it is happening, but a thoughtful process helps you understand the progress and enjoy seeing the home take shape, and when the work is complete, the result should be more than a collection of new materials.

The kitchen may make weekday mornings easier. The bathroom may feel calmer and more organized. A new layout may give everyone room to gather without feeling crowded. Better storage may remove frustrations that had become so familiar you barely noticed them anymore.

The real value is in how the finished space changes everyday life. A well-designed remodel should not feel like someone else’s idea was dropped into your house. It should still feel like your home, only more functional, more comfortable, and better suited to the way your family lives today.

The goal is not only a beautiful finished space, it is an experience that leaves you feeling heard, prepared, and excited to see your home come together.

That is why we believe remodeling should feel like a partnership. At Treasure Valley Redesign & Remodel, we work with homeowners to balance their needs, their dreams, and their budget. Our role is to bring construction knowledge, design experience, planning, and coordination to the ideas and priorities you bring to the project.

Thinking about changing the way your home works? Tell us what is frustrating about your space today and how you hope the space will feel when its finished.

Why Two Remodel Bids Can Look So Different
MAY 22 
WRITTEN BY MICHAEL KUHN
“A good remodel estimate should give you confidence, not confusion.”

If you are planning a remodel, it is normal to talk with more than one contractor. In fact, it is usually a good idea.

A remodel is a big investment. For many homeowners, it may be one of the biggest purchases they make after buying their home. So it makes sense to compare options, ask questions, and make sure you feel comfortable before choosing who to work with.

But comparing remodel bids can be confusing.

Two bids may both say “kitchen remodel,” “bathroom remodel,” or “home addition,” but that does not mean they are pricing the same project.

One bid may include more labor, better materials, more detailed planning, more project management, or more realistic allowances. Another bid may leave some of those things out or push them off until later.

That is why the lowest number is not always the clearest number.

A lower bid is not automatically bad, and a higher bid is not automatically better. The important question is this:

Are the bids actually pricing the same work?

Scope Matters

The first thing to compare is the scope of work.

One contractor may include the full project from start to finish. Another may include only part of the work, or may leave certain pieces vague.

For example, a kitchen remodel might include demo, electrical updates, plumbing adjustments, cabinets, countertops, backsplash, flooring, trim, painting, cleanup, and project management.

Or it might only include some of those things.

If important items are missing, the project may still need them later. That can lead to added invoices, change orders, or decisions that have to be made once the project is already underway.

When comparing remodel bids, ask:

What is included?

And just as important:

What is not included?

A good estimate should help you understand both.

Allowances Can Change the Price

Allowances are another reason remodel bids can look very different.

An allowance is a placeholder amount for something that has not been fully selected yet. This might include cabinets, countertops, tile, flooring, plumbing fixtures, lighting, hardware, or appliances.

Allowances are not bad. They are often necessary early in the process.

But they need to be realistic.

One bid may include a cabinet allowance based on basic stock cabinets. Another may include semi-custom cabinetry with better storage, upgraded finishes, and more custom details.

Both bids may say “cabinets,” but they are not pricing the same product.

The same can happen with tile, countertops, flooring, lighting, fixtures, and other finish materials.

When you are comparing estimates, do not just ask whether an item is included. Ask whether the allowance matches the kind of product you actually want.

Detail Helps Prevent Surprises

A detailed estimate takes time.

It takes time to walk the project, ask questions, understand the goals, think through the unknowns, build realistic allowances, and decide what should be included.

A short bid may be easier to read, but it may not give you enough information to know what you are actually paying for.

A good proposal should help you understand:

What work is included

What materials are being accounted for

What still needs to be selected

What could affect the final price

What assumptions are being made

The goal is not just to give you a number.

The goal is to give you clarity.

Craftsmanship and Project Management Matter

Remodeling is not just about materials. The quality of the labor matters. The trades matter. The installation methods matter. The standards of the company managing the job matter.

Two contractors may both install cabinets, tile, flooring, or trim, but the finished product can be very different.

Project management matters too.

A remodel has a lot of moving pieces. Materials need to be ordered, schedules need to be managed, subcontractors need to be coordinated, inspections need to be handled, and questions need to be answered.

Good project management helps keep the job moving and reduces stress for the homeowner.

When comparing bids, ask:

Who will manage the project?

Who is my main point of contact?

Who coordinates the trades?

Who handles schedule changes?

Who follows through if something needs to be adjusted?

A lower bid may not include the same level of communication, organization, or oversight.

For some homeowners, that may be fine. But for many people, one of the main reasons to hire a general contractor is to have someone managing the whole process for them.

Communication and Trust Matter

A remodel is personal.

You are inviting people into your home. Depending on the size of the project, your contractor may be part of your life for weeks or even months.

That means communication matters.

Before choosing a contractor, ask yourself:

Do I feel comfortable asking questions?

Do I feel heard?

Does this contractor communicate clearly?

Do I understand what is included?

Do I trust this team to handle problems fairly?

Do I feel comfortable having them in my home?

Those things may not show up as a line item on an estimate, but they have a big impact on your experience.

At Treasure Valley Redesign & Remodel, we view remodeling as a partnership. Our goal is not just to finish the project. Our goal is to walk through the process with our clients in a way that feels organized, respectful, and clear.

Questions to Ask When Comparing Remodel Bids

If you are comparing remodel estimates, here are a few helpful questions to ask:

Does each bid include the same scope of work?

What is included?

What is excluded?

Are the allowances realistic?

Are design, plans, permits, or engineering included?

Who orders materials?

Who manages the schedule and subcontractors?

What happens if something changes?

How detailed is the estimate?

What level of communication can I expect?

Do I trust this contractor in my home?

These questions help you compare bids more fairly.

Instead of only asking, “Which bid is lowest?” it is better to ask, “Are these bids actually pricing the same project?”

Final Thoughts

The lowest bid is not always the best value, and the highest bid is not always the best choice.

The real goal is to understand what each contractor is including, what they are leaving out, and how they plan to manage the project.

A good remodel estimate should give you confidence, not confusion.

At Treasure Valley Redesign & Remodel, we want homeowners to understand what is included, what still needs to be finalized, and how different choices can affect the final price.

If you are planning a remodel in the Treasure Valley, we would be happy to talk through your project, answer your questions, and help you understand what to look for as you compare your options.

Why Material Selections Matter Before Final Remodel Pricing
APR 29 
WRITTEN BY MICHAEL KUHN

One of the most exciting parts of planning a remodel is choosing the materials. Cabinets, countertops, tile, flooring, plumbing fixtures, lighting, hardware, paint colors, and grout all help shape the finished look of a space. But selections are not just about design. They also play a major role in final remodel pricing. Early in the remodeling process, many homeowners want to know exactly what their project will cost. That is completely understandable. Budget matters, and it is important to know whether a project makes sense before moving too far forward. However, until materials are selected and the scope is clearly defined, there are usually still several variables that can affect the final price.

Material Choices Affect More Than the Look

A tile selection is not just about color or pattern. The size of the tile, the layout, the grout, the trim pieces, and the installation method can all affect labor and cost. The same is true for many other remodel selections. Cabinet lines, door styles, wood species, countertop materials, flooring types, plumbing fixtures, lighting, appliances, and specialty finishes can all change the final price of a project. For example, two kitchens may have a very similar layout, but the final cost can look different depending on the cabinet selection, countertop material, backsplash design, and finish details. A simple subway tile backsplash will not price the same as a handmade tile, a full-height stone backsplash, or a detailed patterned installation. The overall look matters, but so does the material, the installation process, and the time involved.

Selections Help Create a More Accurate Scope

Before a final remodel proposal is created, the goal is to define the project as clearly as possible. That includes what work is being done, what materials are being used, and what details need to be accounted for. When selections are still undecided, pricing often has to include allowances, placeholders, or assumptions. Those can be helpful early in the planning process, but they are not the same as pricing based on actual selected products.

Finalizing selections helps answer questions such as:

What tile is being installed?

What size and pattern will it be laid in?

What countertop material and edge profile are being used?

What cabinet finish, door style, and layout are selected?

What plumbing and lighting fixtures need to be ordered?

Are there specialty materials with longer lead times?

The more specific those answers are, the more accurate the final proposal can be.

Selections Can Affect Labor, Scheduling, and Lead Times

Material selections also impact the construction schedule. Some products are readily available, while others may take weeks or months to arrive. Custom cabinetry, specialty tile, stone, fixtures, flooring, and appliances can all have lead times that need to be considered before work begins.

Installation requirements matter too. Some materials take more time, more prep, or more specialized labor. A detailed tile pattern, large-format material, natural stone, or custom finish may require additional steps compared to a more standard installation.

This is one reason we encourage homeowners to make selections before construction begins whenever possible. It helps avoid delays, rushed decisions, and unexpected changes once the project is already underway.

A Cohesive Design Starts With Clear Decisions

Product selections are also where the design really starts to come together. Flooring, cabinets, counters, tile, grout, paint, hardware, and lighting all need to work together. When decisions are made one at a time without looking at the full picture, it is easier for the final design to feel disconnected. Taking time to review materials together helps create a more cohesive space. It also gives homeowners a chance to compare options, ask questions, and make decisions with confidence before construction starts.

Better Selections Lead to Better Pricing

The goal of finalizing materials before final pricing is not to make the process more complicated. It is to make the project clearer. When materials are selected early, the proposal can better reflect the actual scope of work. That means fewer assumptions, fewer surprises, and a smoother remodeling process from planning to construction.

If you are thinking about remodeling your home this year, the best time to start planning is before you are ready to begin construction. A little extra time upfront for selections, planning, and pricing can make a big difference once the project starts.

There is something especially pleasing about a before-and-after that completely changes how a space looks, feels, and functions. This kitchen is a perfect example.

When we first saw this space, it had good bones but felt dated and lacked storage, flow, and overall functionality that the homeowners needed. The existing kitchen had older cabinetry, limited workspace, and a layout that did not make the most of the room.

Our goal was to create a kitchen that felt custom, intentional, and much better suited for everyday life.

One of the biggest transformations was the new built-in refrigerator wall. By adding full-height cabinetry and a more integrated design, this area is now a true kitchen feature rather than just an overlooked corner. The added storage and built-in look made a huge impact.

We also reworked the range wall and the long cabinet run at the sink, bringing in new cabinetry, updated finishes, and a much more cohesive design throughout the entire space. The combination of painted cabinets, clean backsplash tile, warm wood flooring, and improved layout gave the kitchen a timeless feel while making it far more functional.

What we love most about this project is how every part of the kitchen now works together. The finished space feels brighter, more polished, and much more custom from one end to the other.

It is hard to believe it is the same kitchen.

If your kitchen looks outdated or no longer works for your family, a thoughtful remodel can make all the difference. Give us a call today to talk about your project. We would love to help you create a space that feels beautiful, functional, and built for the way you live.

The Final 1%: Why Punch Lists Matter
FEB 26 
WRITTEN BY MICHAEL KUHN

If you’ve ever looked at a remodel and thought, “It’s basically done,” there’s a good chance it was actually in the punch list phase.

Punch list is the final stretch of a project. The stage where everything is installed, functioning, and beautiful… and we’re working through the last details that take it from almost finished to fully complete.

That might include:

final paint and caulk touch-ups

Adjusting doors/drawers for a perfect fit

trim details

hardware tweaks

Final walkthrough items

It’s the least “Instagram dramatic” part of construction, but it’s one of the most important.

Why we’re talking about punch lists this week

We’re sharing this photo because this project is about 99% complete, and it’s a great example of what the end of a remodel really looks like.

At the same time, we have another project lined up and ready to move forward, but we’re currently waiting on materials and final selections—specifically the cabinets, which are in production. That’s the part of remodeling that can feel like “hurry up and wait.”

The reality: the timeline isn’t only construction

A remodel timeline is a mix of:

design + decision-making

ordering + lead times

deliveries + coordination

construction + trade sequencing

punch list + closeout

Waiting isn’t always a problem; it’s often the smarter move, especially when it prevents a project from starting and then stalling midstream.

The takeaway

If you’re planning a remodel, remember: the “last 1%” is where the polish happens. And sometimes, the best way to protect the construction timeline is to make sure key selections and materials are locked in before the messy part begins.

If you’re curious how we structure timelines, lead times, and closeout, we’re always happy to walk you through what to expect.

Starting a New Remodel Project: Product Selections
FEB 20 
WRITTEN BY MICHAEL KUHN

One of our favorite parts of any remodel happens before demolition ever begins: product selections.

We’re gearing up to start a new project and have officially begun choosing finishes that will shape the overall look and feel of the space. These early decisions may seem small, but they’re what make a remodel feel cohesive, intentional, and tailored to the homeowner’s style.

A Timeless Pairing: Sage Cabinets + Calacatta-Style Quartz

For this project, we’re loving the direction so far: a soft sage cabinet finish paired with a Calacatta-style quartz. It’s a combination that feels warm and fresh without being trendy.

Why sage cabinetry works so well

Adds color in a calm, grounded way (not too bold, not too neutral)

Pairs beautifully with warm metals, wood tones, and white walls

Holds up visually over time;classic but still interesting

Why Calacatta-style quartz is a go-to

Brightens a space and keeps it feeling open

The veining adds movement without feeling busy

Durable and low-maintenance for everyday life

Together, the green cabinetry and light quartz create a balanced look: inviting, clean, and elevated.

Why Selections Matter Early

Choosing materials early helps us:

Confirm details that affect layout and installation (sizes, edge profiles, appliance specs, hardware spacing)

Avoid delays once construction starts

Keep the overall design consistent from one decision to the next

Selections are also where we can really dial in the homeowner’s goals—whether that’s “timeless and neutral,” “warm and cozy,” or “modern and high contrast.”

What’s Next

Next up is continuing to finalize the full finish palette so everything works together: cabinets, countertops, hardware, lighting, tile, and paint. As the project moves forward, we’ll share more behind-the-scenes moments and progress updates.

If you’re thinking about remodeling this year, the best time to start planning is before you’re ready to start construction. Product availability, lead times, and scheduling all go smoother with a little runway.

Two Months Later: Living in Our Completed Star Remodel
FEB 12 
WRITTEN BY MICHAEL KUHN

Two months have passed since we finished our home remodel in Star and welcomed clients, friends, and family for an open house.

Life has started to settle, and our routines are taking shape. Our family also grew when we welcomed a baby girl just before Christmas.

Bringing a baby into the mix while moving in and getting used to our new space has been a joy. And honestly, there’s no better test for a remodel than coming home with a newborn.

The dust is gone.
The cabinets are full.

Now these spaces support our real life; from late nights and busy mornings to toddlers, bottles, and everything in between.

We’ve realized that the most meaningful part of a remodel isn’t the big reveal. It’s the everyday moments.

What Really Matters After Move-In

Now that we’re back in our newly redesigned home, a few things stand out:

The layout works during busy mornings (which matter more than you think).

The extra space gives us room to breathe with two young kids.

The storage keeps the chaos from taking over.

The lighting and fireplace make late-night feedings feel cozy instead of exhausting.

The materials are holding up beautifully to kids, pets, and daily life.

The choices we made while planning have become part of our routine, and that’s exactly what we hoped for.

What This Project Taught Us

Living through our own remodel (and then bringing a newborn home to it) reminded us of what we always share with our clients:

Thoughtful planning makes all the difference.

Clear communication reduces stress.

Quality craftsmanship is worth it in the long run.

A home should support you through every season of life.

Experiencing it ourselves has made us even more empathetic, and it’s already shaping how we guide and manage projects going forward.

More Than Just a Portfolio Piece

Our home is more than a finished project. It’s where we’re raising our family.

It’s where we wake up to our six-week-old cooing in the morning.
It’s where we hear, “Daddddyyyy… up?” over the monitor.
It’s where we sink into the couch when both girls are finally asleep at the same time, take a deep breath, and feel grateful for the life happening inside these walls.

We want you to feel the same way about your home.

If you’re thinking about remodeling in Star, Eagle, Boise, or anywhere in the Treasure Valley, we’d love to help you plan a project that still feels good long after we’re done.

Because the true success of a remodel isn’t just how it looks in photos. It’s how well it fits your real life.

Behind the Build: Project Complete
JAN 22 
WRITTEN BY MICHAEL KUHN

After months of planning, construction, and countless behind-the-scenes decisions, our Star home remodel is officially complete and we couldn’t be more grateful for how it all came together.

This project was unique in that it was both deeply personal and professionally meaningful. As our own family home, every choice mattered: how the spaces would function day to day, how they would grow with our family, and how they would feel years down the road. At the same time, we approached this renovation exactly the way we approach every client project; with thoughtful design, careful planning, and an unwavering focus on quality craftsmanship.

From the earliest stages of demolition and framing to the final finishes and styling, this remodel allowed us to fully showcase our process. We were intentional about layouts, flow, storage, and materials, making decisions not just for visual impact, but for long-term livability. The result is a home that feels comfortable, timeless, and functional. Designed to support real life, not just look good in photos.

One of the most meaningful moments of this project was our open house, where we had the opportunity to welcome neighbors, friends, clients, and industry partners into our completed space. Being able to walk people through the home, share the story behind the decisions, and celebrate the finish line together was incredibly special. It was a reminder of how much community and trust play a role in what we do.

Throughout this remodel, we shared updates along the way — from early construction milestones to finishing details — with the goal of pulling back the curtain on what a well-run remodel actually looks like. We believe that educated homeowners make confident decisions, and transparency is a key part of a successful project. This home became a real-world example of that philosophy in action.

Now complete, this space reflects everything we strive to create for our clients: homes that are both beautiful and practical, built with care, and tailored to the people who live in them. While this project marks the end of a major chapter for our family, it also serves as a portfolio piece we’re incredibly proud of.

To everyone who followed along, attended the open house, sent encouragement, or supported us throughout this process …. Thank you!! Your support means more than we can say.

If you’re considering a kitchen remodel, bathroom renovation, addition, or whole-home transformation in the Treasure Valley, we’d love to help you bring your vision to life. This project may be finished, but our passion for creating thoughtful, well-built homes continues.

Behind the Build: Countertops, Flooring, & Sneak Peaks
NOV 26 
WRITTEN BY MICHAEL KUHN

Once the paint was up and the tile work was underway, we finally moved into one of my favorite parts of any remodel — the finishes. This is the stage where everything starts feeling intentional, warm, and very much like home.

Countertops: The first big “wow” moment

Countertop install day is always a good day. It’s one of those changes that instantly pulls a space together. The moment the slabs were set in place, the kitchen suddenly looked like the kitchen we had been picturing for months.

Seeing the veining, texture, and color in the actual space — against our paint choices and cabinetry — made the whole design feel real. It was such a rewarding milestone.

Flooring: Bringing warmth and flow

Next came the flooring throughout the addition and remodeled areas. We chose an LVP that felt warm, timeless, and practical (because… kids and dogs 🙃).

As soon as the floors went in, everything changed. The rooms felt grounded and cozy, and the flow from the existing home into the new spaces finally felt seamless. Walking through with continuous flooring made the whole place feel so much bigger and more connected.

Sneak peeks of the finished spaces

With countertops and flooring installed, we finally started seeing small glimpses of the finished home — sunlight on the new floors, countertops meeting the cabinets, fresh paint next to finished trim. These tiny moments made us realize just how close we were to crossing the finish line.

It’s crazy to think how far everything has come in just a few months. Each step brought us closer to creating a home that truly fits our family and showcases the craftsmanship we’re proud to offer our clients every day.

And now… we’re almost there!

We’re officially in the home stretch — installing cabinetry, trim, fixtures, hardware, and tying up all the last details before we open our doors.

If you’re local, we would absolutely love to have you stop by and see the finished remodel in person. It’s been such a labor of love, and we’re so excited to share it with you.

Behind the Build: Drywall, Interior Paint, and Tile Showers
NOV 19 
WRITTEN BY MICHAEL KUHN

After the big push through framing, roofing, and mechanical systems, we finally reached one of the most satisfying stages of any remodel — drywall and interior finishes. This is where the project starts shifting from “construction zone” to “actual home,” and you can suddenly feel the personality of the space begin to take shape.

Drywall: The moment everything feels real

Once mechanical and framing passed inspection, our crew moved straight into hanging and finishing drywall throughout the project. Almost overnight, the house transformed from open studs and exposed wiring into real, livable rooms.

Smooth walls, clean corners, and fully enclosed spaces truly helped transition the project from blueprint to reality — and seeing these walls come together gave us our first real sense of how each space felt. Walking through the playroom, living room, and new primary suite with full walls up was such an exciting milestone.

Interior Paint: Bringing warmth to the walls

With drywall finished, it was time for interior paint — one of the most transformative steps in any remodel. This is where the home begins to develop its mood and character.

We chose colors that reflected the warmth and natural feel we love — tones that pair beautifully with our cabinetry, LVP flooring, tile, and the overall design direction of the home.

The first coat of paint always feels like the home is exhaling — suddenly the rooms brighten, soften, and come to life.

Tile Showers: Craftsmanship meets comfort

Tile is one of those things that instantly changes the feel of a bathroom, and once ours started going up, everything clicked. Seeing the walls come together in the showers — with the layout, spacing, and details falling into place — made the whole area feel pulled together and functional.

Our crew took their time getting everything aligned and laid out the right way — the kind of small details that make a space feel solid and built to last.

By the end of this stage, the house finally started to feel like a home again. With the walls up, fresh paint on every surface, and tile taking shape in the bathrooms, each room felt warm, intentional, and full of possibility. Seeing these pieces come together brought us one big step closer to the space we’ve been dreaming about for so long.

Guided by Craftsmanship

Things were done differently 100 years ago.

While our lifestyles have changed drastically, certain principles still ring true today.

Through our remodel work we shepherd through the best of it; the attention to detail, the quality, and the craftsmanship (it’s in our name).

We believe in timeless design and construction. In any house, vintage or contemporary, the spaces should integrate seamlessly into their surrounds.

Sometimes we wonder, what were they thinking in the 80s?

Process Oriented

At Craftsman Design and Renovation, we partner with you to remodel your Portland, Oregon kitchen, bathroom, basement, or exterior.

With over 25 years of experience, we’ve been around the block a time or two.

We understand the importance of organization, communication, and careful planning during a remodel.

We guide you through our design-build process and are with you every step of the way.

Relationship Focused

As a design-build firm focused in Portland, our goal is to get to know you, your home, and your vision.

Then, we provide you with the best design solutions and build with the highest-quality craftsmanship in the business.

The end result is a better future: for you, your family, and your home.

And you also leave with a lifelong partner in us.

Who We Are

Our passion for history, craftsmanship, and the beauty of old homes in the Portland, Oregon area shines through in everything we do.
We are old house nerds.

We geek out on original woodwork, built-in details, and the perfect rafter tail.

The Tudor, the four square, the bungalow, the craftsman – they are all old friends near and dear to our hearts.

Some clients have called us forensic architects…a new superpower, perhaps? We’ll take it.

As a full service design-build firm in Portland, Oregon we believe in maintaining the architecture and character of our neighborhoods.

We are great teammates.

We take our time through our design process to ensure the end project will fit your lifestyle to a tee.

All our projects are thoughtfully custom.

We talk shower habits, midnight snacking needs, homework routines. No detail is too small.

After design, our production team executes our design vision, while also providing on-site recommendations and solutions.

The bottom line; we’re the kind of teammate you and your home want to have.

We are doers with a plan.

We run a tight ship.

We believe consistency and communication are keys to a successful remodel.

Our communication and quality of work do not waiver, no matter the type of project.

We create a plan, detail it with you, and systematically deliver – time and time again.

You might even miss us when we’re gone.

Now Meet Our Team

Passions: fixing up 1925 home with husband, cooking, grilling & gardening.

Erika Rice, CKBD
Designer

Passions: outdoor adventures (hiking, skiing, kayaking), music, and racing.

Ryan Murphy
Project Manager

Passions: coffee coffee coffee, mountain biking, 80s music.

Bill Myles, CR
Owner

Passions: updating 100 year old home, traveling with family, & time in nature.

Stephanie Capretto, CKBD
Designer

Passions: soccer & softball player, vintage auto lover, proud father.

Pete Kelly, CLC
Lead Carpenter

Passions: sports lover, family focused, outdoor enthusiast.

Nathan Maszy, CLC
Lead Carpenter
Our story: It all started 29 years ago with a love of historic Portland, Oregon and an attic office space. And as they say, the rest is history.
1996
The Beginning

With a passion for Portland’s historic and older homes, Wade Frietag starts Craftsman Design and Renovation out of the attic of his 1905 Craftsman style home.

2004
Leaving the Nest

A bigger team and increased work leads to CDR ‘leaving the nest’ and establishing new offices on SE Division street. The Craftsman Design team continues to grow and expand to take on more projects.

2012
The Growth

 CDR offices are established above Rejuvenation on SE Grand Street in Portland. With shared values of quality craftsmanship, classic design, and excellent customer service it is a perfect match.

2015
The Move

The team moves to SE Belmont Street, in the heart of Southeast Portland. Surrounded by older homes and neighborhoods (as well as great coffee shops to keep the team fueled) this location feels like home.

2026
The Present

Our team continues to be guided by our passion for older homes, and preserving the landscape of Portland. We believe in maintaining the integrity of these beautiful homes, while updating them for today’s living.

What We Do
With superior craftsmanship and a design-build process tailored to your home in Portland, we remodel rooms & exteriors that stand the test of time.
Kitchen Remodeling

Kitchens truly are the heart of the home. They are the entertaining space, the homework zone, the family bonding area and so much more. In older homes, the kitchen can often be a difficult (and smaller) puzzle to solve.

Our comprehensive design-build process really shines in kitchen remodels. We take the time to understand you, your cooking needs and wants, as well as your future goals.

Our goal is to work through a space plan with you to ensure your new custom kitchen will fit your needs perfectly. We guide you through cabinetry, countertop, tile, flooring, and many other decisions.

More Kitchen Remodels >

Bathroom Remodeling

Bathrooms are a space we interact with every single day. With the right design, they can provide calm in the morning and a relaxing sanctuary in the evening.

While a small space in the grand scheme of a home, bathrooms can have a huge impact on how you feel on a daily basis. Having enough storage, a good shower, and room for everyone in the family can have a monumental impact on your day to day experience.

Partnering with us and taking the time to think through your needs and habits ensures that your new custom bathroom will fit you perfectly.

More Bathroom Remodels >

Whole House Remodeling

A whole house remodel can be overwhelming. There are so many parts and pieces to consider, it’s hard to know where to start. That’s why we’re here; to help you every step of the way.

Through our design-build process, we take our time to understand your home and your needs, to ensure the best plan is developed; whether that’s remodeling the whole house at once, or breaking it out in phases as a longer-term, strategic plan.

We approach whole house remodels holistically, determining how each phase will affect the next, to ensure maximum efficiency and minimum stress.

More Whole House Remodels >

Basement Remodeling

The unfinished basement in a home is like a whole new land, waiting to be explored and developed. This is an area where there is some great opportunity to add valuable square footage to your home.

Whether it be more family room space, an extra office, a wine cellar, or another bathroom (hello teenagers), we’ll help guide you through our design-build process to find the best fit for your family’s needs.

Our goal is to build you a space that will blend with the rest of your old home, while gaining additional functionality and space for your family.

More Basement Remodels >

Interior Remodeling

As lovers of older homes, we appreciate the finer details. Original built-ins, wainscot, crown molding…you are speaking our language.

While a lot of our interior remodeling projects are done in conjunction with projects of a larger scope, we are happy to chat with you about the possibilities. We love to see original details restored and carried on for another 100 years.

Our expert team takes the time to observe original detailing and if needed, conduct additional research to make sure what we’re building honors the character of your home.

More Interior Remodels >

Exterior Remodeling

As Portlanders, we are passionate about our city’s landscape and maintaining and preserving the beautiful architecture of our city.

Bearing the Pacific Northwest weather, in addition to years (often over 100) of wear and tear, the exteriors of our homes need some extra care and attention to look and feel their best.

As experts of older homes, we can help you maintain, recreate, or uncover the original exterior beauty of you home.

More Exterior Remodels >

Basement Remodels
Basement Remodeling
A basement remodel is the perfect way to add a little something extra to your home without having to go the route of a home addition. For some homeowners, a basement remodel is an opportunity to add a modern twist to their historical homes by installing a movie theater or game room. For others, it’s a chance to repurpose valuable square footage that they already own and use it to expand their home’s livable space.

For more than two decades, we’ve been helping area residents unlock the hidden potential of their homes with stunning basement remodels and we’d love to do the same for you.

When you partner with us for a basement remodel, our skilled designers will work closely with you to get an understanding of what you hope to accomplish. For instance, are you looking to continue using your basement primarily for laundry and storage? Or, would you like to convert it into livable space that can be used by the whole family? Perhaps you’d like to turn your basement into a guest suite so you can better accommodate overnight visitors?

With the design-build experts at Craftsman, the possibilities for your basement remodel are practically endless. We can work with you to bring your vision to life in a way that satisfies your needs and style preferences.

Whole House Remodels
Whole House Remodeling
Craftsman Design & Renovation is an award-winning
design-build firm that focuses on renovating older homes in the Portland, Oregon area. Not only do we complete basement, bathroom, and kitchen remodels, but if you are looking to restore your entire home, we can provide you with a whole house remodel that will fit your unique needs.

When it comes to remodeling an entire house, creative vision and project management are indispensable, and these are qualities that the Craftsman team brings to every project.

Unlike a one-room remodel, a whole house remodel requires a comprehensive design approach to ensure that the end result blends seamlessly together and looks like a unified whole. We can perform a study of your home and compare it to other nearby houses that were built around the same time to get an understanding of the architectural and design trends that were popular at that time. We will use these trends to guide your project while also taking into consideration your unique tastes and style preferences.

Addition Remodels
Addition Remodeling

Here at Craftsman Design and Renovation we take pride in our meticulous approach to preserving the character of older homes while seamlessly integrating modern amenities. 

Completing an old home addition requires a delicate balance between honoring the original architecture and meeting the needs of contemporary living. A skilled craftsman understands the historical significance of the property and strives to enhance its charm while adding functional space.

In blending the addition with the age of the home, attention to detail is paramount. This involves meticulous craftsmanship to match architectural features, such as trim work, molding, and materials, to those found in the existing structure. We guide you through these decisions during our design process, and execute with expert craftsmanship during our build process.

The result is a cohesive and timeless space that respects the home’s heritage while providing modern comfort and functionality, creating a living environment that feels both rooted in history and tailored for the present day.

Exterior Remodels
Exterior Remodeling
If you’re considering remodeling the exterior of your home, you’ll want to partner with a company that has ample experience working with your specific style of house. This is especially the case if you want to preserve or restore specific architectural details. Since 1996, countless homeowners in the Portland, Oregon area have turned to the team at Craftsman Design & Renovation for historically-sensitive remodels.

Known industry-wide for our impeccable workmanship and extensive knowledge of architecture and design trends, we are committed to providing every customer we serve with a truly wonderful home improvement experience.

When you contact us, we’ll begin by scheduling a free design consultation during which one of our knowledgeable designers will work closely with you to gain a better understanding of what kind of exterior home remodeling project you have in mind.

Once you sign a design agreement, we will begin drafting preliminary architectural drawings and produce a 3-D rendering to give you an idea of what your finished project will look like. After all the details are finalized, our expert team will go to work, adhering closely to a construction timeline to ensure that your project is completed on time.

Our Design-Build Process
Partnering through our Design-Build
process guides us to practical and thoughtful
solutions for you and your home.

Phase One: We Partner


In-Home or Online Consultation Initial evaluation of project with homeowner to determine if we are a good fit for each other.



Design Agreement Flexible design retainer which expands or contracts based on your needs, with realistic target budget.



Project Survey On-site measure, evaluation, photography, and design goal interview to clearly understand objectives.

Phase Two: We Design


Concept Design Creative exploration of design options, based on project survey with floor plans, 3D drawings, and refined target budget.

R

Design Development Consolidation of concept designs along with initial fixture and finish selections. Preliminary estimate presented with detailed scope of work.

i

Contract Documents Finalize fixture and finish selections, conduct trade walk-through, and develop contract documents. Health & Safety plan is reviewed.

Phase Three: We Prepare


Construction Agreement Fixed cost construction agreement with approved drawings, selections, and Health & Safety Plan.



Permit Drawing Review final details, verify dimensions, orders and selections. Submit permit set with engineering (if required) and construction details.



Design to Production Hand-Off Construction prestart meeting with Production Manager, Project Manager, and on-site Lead Carpenter.

Phase Four: We build


Job Site Set Up The construction area is sealed off, reducing noise and exposure to the rest of the home.



Daily Cleanings Jobsites are left broom clean at the end of every workday. All staff follow Health & Safety Plan procedures.



Weekly Meetings Lead Carpenter communicates regularly with homeowners to update on project status, questions, and schedule.

Beautiful Remodel Complete
Get started building your dream project today

Our team is here and ready to assist you in creating the best space for you. We can guide you through a kitchen, bathroom, basement, exterior, or even a whole house project. 

As a design-build firm in Portland, Oregon, our thorough and honest approach to design allows less stress and surprises on your end, and gives you the home you’ve always wanted.

CALL 503.239.6200
REQUEST A CONSULTATION
Here’s what our process looks like.
WHAT
OUR
CLIENTS
SAY

Craftsman recently completed a kitchen renovation in our 1911 Craftsman, and also moved our washer and dryer from the basement onto our second floor. In short, we could not be more satisfied with the project from beginning to end and we would not want to work with anyone else but Craftsman for any future renovations. We are in love with the quality, beauty and craftsmanship of our kitchen and know it will remain for at least another 100 years. We felt comfortable and supported by everyone at Craftsman, and enjoyed spending time with them throughout the process.
JEN

1902 NW Craftsman Kitchen

In this 1902 NW Craftsman kitchen, thoughtful layout changes brought new life and flow to the heart of the home. Relocating the powder bath door opened up a range of design possibilities, allowing for better circulation and a new peninsula for prep and seating. Original millwork details were carefully replicated, including stained wood, v-groove wainscot, and custom leaded glass transom windows that echo the home’s historic charm. A dramatic soapstone countertop—chosen for its striking, vein-like pattern—became the focal point. Finishing touches like black-and-white hex tile and playful wallpaper add character to this fresh yet timeless renovation.

OUR HOME REMODELING PROCESS

At GMH Construction we use a three-step approach to help homeowners understand their options, improve the accuracy of project cost prior to the construction contract, and ultimately, maximize the return on the investment for the homeowner.

Step 1: Consultation

Meeting to discuss your project at your home allows us to identify the scope of the job and discuss pre-construction and renovation processes. We will then contact you for a follow-up appointment in approximately 2 to 3 weeks to present a Design Retainer. The Design Retainer outlines the scope of work, project budget range, and estimated engagement time with our designers.

Step 2: The Design Process

The Design Retainer allows us to design intelligently and accurately estimate the project cost. This important work has great value: accurate budgets, excellent design, maximum return on investment, better planning by the contractor, and better decision-making by the homeowner. A well-designed and well-built home is less expensive to live in, maintain, heat, and cool.

Our designers will guide you through the decision-making and selection process to achieve your renovation goals. By the end of the design process, we will have a finalized budget and scope of work to create a detailed Construction Contract.

Step 3: Construction Contract

Signing the Construction Contract is the final step which includes scheduling a start date for your project. We pride ourselves on creating accurate contracts, realistic schedules, and good quality control to assure outstanding results. For most projects, we have a fixed price contract, which outlines the scope of work to be completed, and the cost to complete the job.

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
What time do the crews work?

We generally begin our day at 7:00 and end at 4:00. However, we work with each client to determine good starting times for their family.

Who will be supervising my job?

One of the owners, Greg or Dane, will come and meet with you to discuss your ideas, plan your project and write your bid. During the design process Robin or Audrey, and their team of design/construction professionals will work with you to design, specify and price your project.

When you decide to start the project, Greg and Dane will consistently be present at your home throughout the remodeling process to assure quality workmanship, accurate implementation of the contract and that you are always satisfied with the work. Remember Greg and Dane are always available to you by cell phone.

We love our new kitchen!

From the moment, we sat down with Greg, we trusted him and knew that he was our contractor.
He was meticulous in taking measurements and making sure he understood what we were looking for. This was important because we wanted a wall removed, storage created, and relevant function in our kitchen. The second time we met with Greg, he had a machine-prepared sketch of our home so we could conceptualize the placement of cabinets, appliances, and lighting.
As it turned out, he, his team, and his suppliers exceeded our expectations while keeping costs close to our budget.
When the cabinet costs seemed to take off to the stratosphere, he found a solution that allowed us to have the wood we chose and still have the quality we wanted. Greg did not just turn us over to a cabinet supplier, he was there in the meeting when we hit a bump in the road.
The sub-contractors previewed the work and showed up on time to keep the process moving. They were professional as well as friendly with our very inquisitive dog.
Every day, the crew cleaned up so we could continue to live in the house during major construction. GMH also uses a unique air filtering device. It is a super-giant HEPA filter that keeps the dust down in the rest of the house.
The craftsmanship was better than we could have ever hoped. Their carpenters are true woodworkers and pay meticulous attention to the tightness of joints and finished color in all light situations. The detailed method they used was far beyond our expectations.
I don’t think we had many changes to the original plan, but GMH was quick to respond and discuss cost impacts.
There were recommendations by GMH that we had never considered and made our new kitchen complete and enjoyable. The richness added by the addition of furniture ends to our cabinets is more than we could have ever hoped for.
The project was completed in less than their anticipated timeline which was a big bonus for us.
I should mention that being a NARI contractor, they were sure to have all the necessary permits from the city and the inspectors were scheduled so as not to cause a delay in the project.
We were so impressed by every facet of GMH, that we had them do our bathroom while we went on vacation. Once again, they exceeded our expectations and the bathroom is stunning.
We cannot thank Greg and his team enough. We have lived in this house for 28 years and now parts of it are not only brand new but luxuriously too.

Dennis J.

Kitchen Remodeling

Introducing GMH Remodeling, your professional partner in reinventing and designing your kitchen space. Serving cities throughout Southeastern Wisconsin, we strive to turn every kitchen remodel concept into a meticulously designed, fully functional kitchen that seamlessly blends with your lifestyle and home aesthetics.

UNLEASHING THE POTENTIAL OF YOUR KITCHEN WITH GMH REMODELING

Every kitchen holds the promise of transforming into a dynamic, efficient space that caters to all your culinary needs while showcasing your personal style. Our expert kitchen modelers unlock this potential with our advanced kitchen remodeling services, breathing new life into your existing kitchen environment.

Contact Us

Have a Look at Our Gallery of Recent Kitchen Remodel Projects Here

COMPREHENSIVE KITCHEN REMODELING COMPONENTS
Customized Kitchen Cabinets

Cabinets serve as the backbone of your kitchen remodel. They significantly contribute to the overall aesthetics and functionality of your space. Our skilled kitchen remodeling contractors leverage their design expertise to create and install bespoke cabinets. These custom cabinets are designed with utmost precision, ensuring they blend flawlessly with your kitchen’s layout and cater to your storage requirements.

Luxurious Countertops

A kitchen remodel transcends completion with the installation of elegant countertops. As a leading kitchen remodeling company, we bring a broad spectrum of countertop options to the table, catering to diverse design preferences and budgets. Our home improvement veterans walk you through the process of selecting the perfect countertop that enhances your kitchen’s beauty while elevating its practical utility.

Functional and Beautiful Kitchen Islands

An appropriately designed kitchen island can revolutionize your kitchen space, lending it a unique character. Our team of kitchen remodelers collaborates with you, assimilating your requirements and style to design a kitchen island that not only complements your kitchen remodel but significantly boosts your kitchen workflow.

Modern Kitchen Lighting Solutions

Effective lighting forms the lifeblood of a warm, inviting kitchen. Our kitchen restorers ensure your kitchen remodel embodies the ideal balance of ambient, task, and accent lighting to curate the perfect atmosphere and practical functionality in your space.

Durable and Attractive Flooring Options

As a full-fledged kitchen remodeling service, we provide a myriad of flooring alternatives. These span across various styles, textures, and durability levels. Our kitchen remodeling experts assist you in making an informed choice, leading you to a flooring solution that is as attractive as it is robust and low-maintenance.

Smart Storage and Organization Solutions

An intelligent storage and organization plan is the cornerstone of a successful kitchen remodel. Our designs incorporate clever storage solutions, enabling you to maintain an organized, clutter-free kitchen. By maximizing the utilization of your kitchen space, we ensure your remodel aligns with your lifestyle and storage needs.

OUR KITCHEN REMODELING PROJECTS
POPULAR KITCHEN STYLES FOR YOUR REMODEL

Choosing a style for your kitchen remodel can significantly shape the overall ambiance and functionality of your space. It’s more than just aesthetics; it’s about creating a room that harmoniously fits with your home’s architecture and your lifestyle. Here, we share some popular kitchen styles that you can consider for your remodel:

OUR KITCHEN REMODELING OPTIONS

Standard kitchen remodels include upgraded plumbing fixtures, cabinets, granite countertops, tile flooring, and more. It may also include some minor wall modifications and moving of fixtures/appliances.

The average cost of a standard kitchen remodel will range between $75,000 – $100,000+.

The time to complete the project can be between 12-16+ weeks.

WHY CHOOSE GMH REMODELING FOR YOUR KITCHEN RENOVATION

Choosing a kitchen remodeling contractor is a significant decision. As expert kitchen remodelers offering a proven process to turn your ideas into reality, we appreciate the uniqueness of each kitchen renovation project. We offer a tailored service portfolio designed to meet your distinct needs, ultimately delivering a kitchen that resonates with your vision and stands the test of time.

Expertise & Experience: With over 30 years in the home remodeling business, GMH Construction, Inc. is your trusted choice for all aspects of your home remodeling project.
Customized Designs: Our team of experienced and creative interior designers works closely with you to transform your living space with stunning designs tailored to your unique style.
Quality Craftsmanship: Our premium materials & skilled craftsmen guarantee lasting results.
Attention to Detail: With an eye for detail, we guide you through every step of the interior design process.
Timely Completion: Our efficient project management ensures that timelines are met, allowing you to enjoy your newly renovated kitchen as soon as possible.
Transparent Communication: We keep you informed at every stage of the remodeling process, addressing any concerns promptly and ensuring a smooth and stress-free experience.
Customer Satisfaction: Customer satisfaction is at the heart of everything GMH Construction does. We prioritize your needs and preferences, going above and beyond to exceed expectations and deliver quality results.
Southeastern Wisconsin service: GMH Construction regularly remodels kitchens in cities like New Berlin, Waukesha, Brookfield, Elm Grove and beyond.
WHY COMMUNICATION MATTERS DURING A REMODEL

Remodeling projects involve hundreds of moving parts, from design decisions and material deliveries to trade scheduling and inspections. Questions and unexpected situations are inevitable. The strongest projects aren’t necessarily the ones without challenges—they’re the ones where homeowners and contractors communicate openly and address issues quickly.

The team at GMH uses JobTread for consistent communication that reaches multiple team members simultaneously resulting in quicker, more collaborative response. If the situation is an emergency, we can always be reached by phone.

Don’t be afraid to ask questions, share concerns, or seek clarification. A good remodeling team wants you informed and comfortable throughout the process. Clear communication helps prevent misunderstandings, reduces stress, and keeps everyone working toward the same goal.

Transitional Style Bathroom

The Transitional style combines the warmth of traditional design and the sleekness of contemporary style, creating a timeless bathroom space.

Spa Style Bathroom

The Spa style transforms your bathroom into a personal sanctuary with the use of calming colors, luxurious tubs, and high-end fixtures.

Industrial Style Bathroom

For a raw and rugged aesthetic, the Industrial style features elements like exposed brick, stainless steel fixtures, and a warehouse-inspired look.

Farmhouse-style bathrooms are characterized by their use of natural materials, free-standing tubs, open shelving, and a homely, rustic charm.

Our team of basement remodeling pros specializes in installing and upgrading bathrooms, all in line with your preferences and budget. As part of our promise to offer excellent value, we provide quality workmanship and materials, ensuring longevity and a seamless finish. Check out our testimonials.

A full basement remodel can cost anywhere from $90,000 to $120,000+ per 1,000 square feet. The cost of a basement remodel largely depends on your budget and the finish materials you choose. For the most accurate price estimate for your basement remodeling project, contact GMH Construction.
